topic: Law change: Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 notified by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, replacing the Aircraft Rules, 1937, from 1 Jan 2027 - Rule 192: airlines must show the total fare with a full break-up (base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges, refund conditions), file tariffs with DGCA; Centre may issue proportionate, time-limited fare directions in extraordinary situations; no fare cap

slides.title: New rules for **flight fares** from 2027
slides.subtitle: Airlines must show the **full price** and its **break-up** before you pay.
slides.cite: **Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026** · Rule 192 · in force from **1 Jan 2027**

slides.label: What has changed
slides.title: A **new rulebook** for aviation
bullets: The Ministry of Civil Aviation has notified the **Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026**.
It replaces the nearly 90-year-old **Aircraft Rules, 1937** and takes effect from **1 January 2027**.
It covers safety, licensing, airports and also how airlines **publish fares**.

slides.label: What you will see
slides.title: No more **hidden charges**
bullets: Fares must be published on airline **websites and apps**.
The **total amount payable** must be shown while booking and on the **ticket**.
Separate break-up of **base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges** and **refund conditions**. Government taxes must be shown apart from airline fees.

slides.label: Who keeps watch
slides.title: DGCA monitors, **Centre can step in**
bullets: Airlines set fares based on factors like **operating cost** and must file tariff details with the **DGCA**.
In an **extraordinary situation**, the Centre can issue written directions on fares in the **public interest**.
Such directions must be **proportionate** and last only for a **specified period**.
slides.note: **Law fact:** the old Rule 135(4) named **excessive or predatory pricing**; reports say the new Rule 192 does not list these grounds.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: This is **not** a fare cap
bullets: There is **no ceiling** on ticket prices. Airlines still set fares by demand and cost, as they have since **1994**.
The new rules apply only from **1 January 2027**, not to this festive season.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Ever booked a flight and found extra charges at the last step? New rules aim to fix that ✈️⚖️

The Ministry of Civil Aviation has notified the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026. These rules replace the Aircraft Rules, 1937 and come into force on 1 January 2027. Along with safety, licensing and airports, they also deal with how airlines show their fares.

Under Rule 192, airlines must publish fares on their websites and apps, show the total amount payable while booking and on the ticket, and give a separate break-up of base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges and refund conditions. Airlines must file tariff details with the DGCA, which will monitor fares. In an extraordinary situation, the Centre can issue written directions on fares in the public interest, but they must be proportionate and only for a specified period.

Please note: there is no cap on ticket prices. Airlines still set their own fares, as they have since 1994. Reports also point out that the old rule's specific mention of excessive or predatory pricing does not appear in the new Rule 192. The new rules do not apply to this festive season.

Law: Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 (Rule 192), Ministry of Civil Aviation, in force from 1 Jan 2027
